TL;DR: The paper proposes STAITUS, a framework for unsupervised video object tracking that disentangles object representation into appearance and geometric pose, improving tracking stability and segmentation quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current slot-based methods for unsupervised video object tracking struggle with entangled appearance and pose, leading to inconsistent object identities and fragmented objects.

Method: STAITUS explicitly disentangles each slot into appearance and geometric pose, enforcing spatial separation within frames and applying temporal alignment only in appearance space.

Result: STAITUS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in segmentation quality and tracking stability on synthetic and real-world benchmarks.

Conclusion: The proposed STAITUS framework effectively addresses the limitations of current slot-based methods, providing a more robust and accurate approach to unsupervised video object tracking.

Abstract: Unsupervised video object tracking aims to decompose dynamic scenes into persistent, object-centric entities without manual annotations. Many recent approaches rely on slot-based representations, where a fixed set of latent variables ("slots") represent individual objects across frames. To preserve object identity, these models enforce temporal consistency on slot embeddings. However, when appearance and pose are entangled, this consistency objective conflicts with object motion and viewpoint changes. As a result, slots tend to lock onto static regions (e.g., background) to satisfy the consistency objective, while foreground objects become fragmented across multiple slots or frequently swap identities. To address these limitations, we propose STAITUS, a unified framework that explicitly disentangles each slot into appearance and geometric pose (position/scale). Leveraging this disentanglement, STAITUS enforces within-frame spatial separation and applies temporal alignment only in appearance space, yielding sharper masks and more persistent identities under motion, occlusion, and object entry/exit. Furthermore, to mitigate over-segmentation, we introduce an adaptive gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts the number of active slots to match scene complexity. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that STAITUS substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in segmentation quality and tracking stability.

</details>


### [263] [MeGAS: Thermomechanical Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Thermophysical Scene Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23455)
*Zesong Yang,Yuanhang Lei,Liyuan Cui,Yihang Chen,Jiaer Huang,Boming Zhao,Peter Yichen Chen,Hujun Bao,Zhaopeng Cui*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A novel framework called MeGAS is proposed, integrating thermomechanical phase-change dynamics into 3D Gaussian Splatting for more realistic and physically plausible simulations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing approaches to scene reconstruction and animation neglect temperature, a crucial physical factor in phenomena like melting and solidification.

Method: MeGAS uses a thermomechanical dynamic Gaussian Splatting representation, a heat advection-diffusion solver with MPM dynamics, and a topology-adaptive Gaussian rendering strategy.

Result: MeGAS produces physically consistent thermomechanical behavior and high-fidelity photorealistic rendering.

Conclusion: MeGAS advances toward physics-integrated world models by incorporating thermomechanical phase-change dynamics into 3D Gaussian Splatting.

Abstract: Recent advances integrate physically grounded Newtonian dynamics with neural rendering frameworks, narrowing the gap between photorealistic scene reconstruction and physics-based animation. However, existing approaches focus on mechanically driven dynamics while neglecting temperature, a fundamental yet invisible physical factor underlying phenomena such as melting, solidification, and other thermomechanical processes. In this paper, we propose MeGAS, a novel framework that incorporates thermomechanical phase-change dynamics into 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Specifically, we propose a new thermomechanical dynamic Gaussian Splatting representation that augments 3DGS with temperature attributes and employs a heat advection-diffusion solver with MPM dynamics incorporating phase transitions, enabling physically plausible and visually realistic synthesis of thermophysical phenomena. Furthermore, a new topology-adaptive Gaussian rendering strategy is proposed to mitigate cracking and floaters under extreme deformation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeGAS produces physically consistent thermomechanical behavior while maintaining high-fidelity photorealistic rendering, advancing toward physics-integrated world models.

</details>


### [264] [C^2GR: Coupled Comprehensive Generative Replay for a Continually Learnable Universal Segmentation Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23473)
*Wei Li,Jingyang Zhang,Guoan Wang,Junzhi Ning,Yang Chen,Guang Yang,Lixu Gu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A novel framework called Coupled Comprehensive Generative Replay (C^2GR) is proposed to address the problem of forgetting in task-incremental learning for universal segmentation models, achieving a 2.44% drop in overall performance compared to joint training.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Universal segmentation models face the challenge of forgetting previous tasks when learning new tasks sequentially, especially when tasks have different imaging modalities and segmentation objectives.

Method: The C^2GR framework, which includes a Bayesian Joint Diffusion (BJD) method for preserving image-mask correspondence and a Relation-aware Unified Prompt Synchronization (RUPS) scheme for synchronizing generator and segmentor optimization.

Result: C^2GR exhibits only a 2.44% drop in overall performance compared to joint training with all task data, effectively alleviating forgetting from concurrent shifts.

Conclusion: The proposed C^2GR framework effectively mitigates forgetting in task-incremental learning for universal segmentation models, demonstrating its potential for diverse tasks involving different imaging modalities and segmentation objectives.

Abstract: Universal segmentation models exhibit significant potential for diverse tasks involving different imaging modalities and segmentation objectives. Task-Incremental Learning provides a privacy-preserving approach to continually evolve a universal model on tasks from sequentially-arriving medical departments. However, training the model solely on the incoming task induces forgetting on past tasks, since consecutive tasks exhibit concurrent shifts in image appearance and segmentation objective. To address this problem, we propose a novel Coupled Comprehensive Generative Replay (C^2GR) framework that simultaneously synthesizes image-mask pairs of previous tasks to mitigate forgetting under concurrent appearance and objective shifts. This requires preserving image-mask correspondence for structure-realistic generation and bridging asynchronous optimization of the generator and segmentor for segmentation-oriented generation. Specifically, we propose a Bayesian Joint Diffusion (BJD) method that formulates the correspondence as conditional distributions optimized via conditional denoising. Furthermore, we develop a Relation-aware Unified Prompt Synchronization (RUPS) scheme to simultaneously modulate the generator and segmentor via a shared task-relation-aware prompt for synchronizing their optimization. Experiments on 20 tasks spanning diverse modalities and objectives demonstrate that C^2GR exhibits only a 2.44% drop in overall performance compared to joint training with all task data, effectively alleviating forgetting from the concurrent shifts. Our code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/mar-cry/C2GR.

</details>


### [265] [From Reconstruction to Decision: A Post-Encoder Plug-in Adapter for Curvilinear Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23486)
*Qin Lei,Jiang Zhong,Xin Xiao,Yuming Yang,Hao Wu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A lightweight post-encoder adapter, PEPA, is proposed to improve curvilinear object segmentation by addressing reconstruction and decision bottlenecks, yielding consistent improvements in topological connectivity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Curvilinear object segmentation is challenging due to spatial sparsity and topological fragility, and modern segmentation pipelines rely on strong but hard-to-modify foundation encoders.

Method: PEPA, a post-encoder plug-in adapter, is introduced with two components: Target-Conditioned Snake Upsampling (TCSU) and Target-Adaptive Differentiable Thresholding (TADT).

Result: Experiments on five benchmarks show that adding PEPA to frozen-encoder baselines yields consistent improvements in topological connectivity, with gains in clDice exceeding those in IoU.

Conclusion: PEPA offers a practical post-encoder enhancement for structure-centric segmentation with only ~0.26M additional parameters, improving structural continuity in curvilinear object segmentation.

Abstract: Curvilinear object segmentation, including vessels and cracks, is challenging due to extreme spatial sparsity and topological fragility, where small local errors can cause severe structural disconnections. Meanwhile, modern segmentation pipelines increasingly rely on strong but hard-to-modify foundation encoders whose heavy downsampling limits fine structural recovery. Motivated by this, we focus on the post-encoder stage and study two recurring and actionable failure modes: a reconstruction bottleneck in high-resolution feature restoration and a decision bottleneck in binarization. We present PEPA, a lightweight Post-Encoder Plug-in Adapter for 2D curvilinear segmentation pipelines with accessible decoder/head features and target, query, or class descriptors. PEPA couples (i) Target-Conditioned Snake Upsampling (TCSU), which uses target-conditioned continuous snake-like sampling to better recover thin and tortuous structures during upsampling, and (ii) Target-Adaptive Differentiable Thresholding (TADT), which predicts target-specific thresholds and optimizes a soft-threshold surrogate with explicit safeguards against trivial bias shifting. Under this post-encoder interface, PEPA can be attached to both prompt-based decoders and conventional dense predictors. Experiments on five medical and industrial benchmarks show that adding PEPA to frozen-encoder baselines yields consistent improvements, with gains in topological connectivity (clDice) typically exceeding those in region overlap (IoU), indicating improved structural continuity. With only $\sim$0.26M additional parameters, PEPA offers a practical post-encoder enhancement for structure-centric segmentation.

</details>


### [266] [Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23494)
*Zhenyu Yi,Zhiyun Song,Yusong Sun,Zelin Liu,Manman Fei,Zhenhao Li,Jiaxuan Zhao,Xu Han,Lichi Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper proposes Brain-Adapter, a novel framework for automated diagnosis of 3D brain CT scans using pre-trained 2D vision-language models and raw diagnostic reports.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The heavy reliance on manual annotations and limited semantic understanding of conventional models make automated diagnosis of 3D brain CT scans challenging.

Method: Brain-Adapter uses a dual-stream multiple instance learning framework with a Text-Conditioned Attention mechanism and a parallel visual MIL stream, supervised by structured labels extracted via a Large Language Model.

Result: The method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL approaches, providing a highly scalable and clinically viable solution for 3D acute intracranial pathology analysis.

Conclusion: Brain-Adapter eliminates the reliance on dense annotations and offers a robust scan-level multi-label classification solution for automated diagnosis of 3D brain CT scans.

Abstract: Automated diagnosis of 3D brain CT scans is essential for critical care, yet it remains challenging due to the heavy reliance on manual annotations and the limited semantic understanding of conventional models. While 2D foundation vision-language models (VLMs) have shown remarkable generalization, effectively transferring their representational power to 3D volumes remains an open problem. In this paper, we propose Brain-Adapter, a novel dual-stream multiple instance learning (MIL) framework that leverages pre-trained 2D biomedical VLMs and raw diagnostic reports for robust scan-level multi-label classification. Specifically, we introduce a Text-Conditioned Attention (TCA) mechanism, utilizing raw diagnostic sentences as semantic queries to dynamically align visual cues with specific disease concepts. Concurrently, a parallel visual MIL stream captures global scan characteristics, supervised by structured labels extracted via a Large Language Model (LLM). To ensure representation coherence, a consistency constraint enforces synergy between the two streams. During inference, an Uncertainty-Aware Refinement (UAR) module dynamically calibrates and fuses these dual-stream predictions to resolve ambiguous cases. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL approaches. By eliminating the reliance on dense annotations, Brain-Adapter provides a highly scalable and clinically viable solution for 3D acute intracranial pathology analysis.

</details>


### [267] [UniverSat: Resolution- and Modality-Agnostic Transformers for Earth Observation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23503)
*Yohann Perron,Guillaume Astruc,Nicolas Gonthier,Clement Mallet,Loic Landrieu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A new Vision Transformer (ViT) model called UniverSat is proposed for Earth Observation (EO) tasks, which can handle varied input modalities, scales, and resolutions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The reliance on rigid patch projectors in existing ViT models hinders their transfer to EO tasks where input modalities, scales, and resolutions vary widely.

Method: UniverSat uses a Universal Patch Encoder to map patches from arbitrary spatial, spectral, and temporal resolutions into a shared embedding space with a shared set of weights.

Result: The proposed approach yields strong results across classification and segmentation on standard EO benchmarks from GeoBench, PANGEABench, and SpectralEarth.

Conclusion: The UniverSat model enables training a single model on heterogeneous multimodal corpora via self-supervision, yielding robust, sensor-agnostic spatial features.

Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViT) dominate computer vision. However, their reliance on rigid patch projectors hinders transfer to Earth Observation (EO), where input modalities, scales, and resolutions vary widely. We introduce UniverSat, a ViT-style backbone built around a Universal Patch Encoder that maps patches from arbitrary spatial, spectral, and temporal resolutions, and from both optical and non-optical sensors, into a shared embedding space with a shared set of weights. This enables training a single model on heterogeneous multimodal corpora via self-supervision, yielding robust, sensor-agnostic spatial features. We validate this approach with strong results across classification and segmentation on standard EO benchmarks from GeoBench, PANGEABench, and SpectralEarth. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/gastruc/UniverSat.

</details>


### [268] [Arbor: Explicit Geometric Conditioning for Controllable 3D Asset Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23514)
*Jan-Niklas Dihlmann,Andreas Engelhardt,Simon Donne,Hendrik P. A. Lensch,Mark Boss*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Arbor is a trainable attachment for text-conditioned 3D generation that introduces a native 3D control interface using constraint meshes, allowing for explicit control over object spatial intent.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current text and image conditioned 3D models lack direct control over object spatial intent, making it difficult to author objects with specific spatial requirements.

Method: Arbor uses constraint meshes as a control interface, converting them into tokens and learning a routed attachment inside a frozen denoiser to incorporate spatial constraints into 3D generation.

Result: Arbor improves constraint obedience while preserving object quality and variation under fixed constraints, even without dedicated compliance losses.

Conclusion: The proposed Arbor method provides an effective way to incorporate explicit spatial constraints into text-conditioned 3D generation, improving control over object spatial intent.

Abstract: Text and image conditioned 3D models now generate convincing assets, but they still offer little direct control over the space an object should occupy or avoid. In authoring, this spatial intent is often known before generation starts. A chair should fit a seating envelope, a prop should leave clearance for motion, or a part should expose a contact surface. Prompts and image views are poor carriers for such constraints, requiring the need for an explicit control interface.
  We present Arbor, a trainable attachment for text conditioned latent 3D generation. Arbor introduces constraint meshes as a native 3D control interface. The interface uses hull regions where geometry should exist, avoidance regions that should remain empty, and touch regions the object should contact. Unlike completion or whole object scaffold control, these meshes are not target evidence. They are local typed requirements and can include regions where no surface should appear. Arbor keeps this signal as geometry by converting constraint meshes into tokens and learning a routed attachment inside a frozen denoiser. Each latent region can therefore receive the part of the constraint that matters for its spatial location.
  We evaluate Arbor on automatic and artist curated control benchmarks with hull, avoidance, and touch constraints, and compare the metric trends to a user preference study. Even without dedicated compliance losses, Arbor improves constraint obedience while preserving object quality and variation under fixed constraints.

</details>


### [269] [Scaling State-Space Models from Lines to Paragraphs: An Ablation of Mamba-based OCR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23524)
*Merveilles Agbeti-Messan,Pierrick Tranouez,Stéphane Nicolas,Clément Chatelain,Thierry Paquet*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The study examines the scalability of a Mamba-based OCR recognizer for transcribing long text sequences, comparing its performance to a Transformer baseline.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to investigate the effectiveness of State-Space Models (SSMs) like Mamba for end-to-end OCR, particularly for long, paragraph-level text, and to understand their behavior and limitations.

Method: The study conducts a systematic exploration of four core hyperparameters of the Mamba-based recognizer on synthetic paragraphs and compares its performance to a Transformer baseline on both synthetic and real handwriting data.

Result: The Mamba-based recognizer achieves comparable accuracy to the Transformer baseline on clean synthetic paragraphs, with a significant speedup, but lags behind on real handwriting data, with a substantial performance gap attributed to data scarcity.

Conclusion: The study concludes that SSMs like Mamba are a practical choice for large-scale document transcription when data is abundant, but may not be suitable when data is scarce, particularly for handwriting recognition.

Abstract: End-to-end OCR increasingly relies on autoregressive sequence models, where the quadratic cost of Transformer attention limits efficient transcription of long, paragraph-level text. State-Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer linear-time decoding and have recently been shown to match Transformer accuracy on printed historical lines, but their behavior as sequences grow from short lines to full paragraphs, and their generalization to handwriting, remain poorly understood. We study how a Mamba-based OCR recognizer scales from lines to paragraphs. We first conduct a systematic exploration of its four core hyperparameters (decoder depth, state dimension, expansion factor, and connector depth) on synthetic paragraphs from 100 to 1,000 characters, identifying the recurrent state dimension and the expansion factor as the dominant levers for long-sequence accuracy. We then compare the recognizer against a Transformer baseline trained under an identical protocol. On clean synthetic paragraphs, both models stay below 1% CER at every length while the SSM runs 1.4 to 4.5 times faster, the speedup growing with sequence length. On real handwriting, however, the SSM lags clearly behind: it reaches 8.2% CER on IAM lines and 10.0% on IAM paragraphs, against 4.2% and 3.5% for the Transformer baseline. Through controlled experiments we show that a substantial part of this gap stems from data scarcity rather than from an intrinsic architectural limit: the autoregressive SSM decoder is markedly data-hungry on long sequences. Our study clarifies when SSMs are a practical choice for large-scale document transcription and when they are not.

</details>


### [270] [LightSTAR: Efficient Visual Document Retrieval via Lightweight Selection with Vision-Adaptive Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23539)
*Tongkun Guan,Haocheng Wang,Wei Shen,Xiaokang Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper proposes LightSTAR, an efficient framework for visual document retrieval that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing latency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Visual document retrieval is challenging due to the need for rapid location of relevant pages from large multi-modal corpora, and existing methods using Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are computationally expensive.

Method: The proposed LightSTAR framework consists of two stages: 1) LLM-free Visual Selection, which uses content-grounded query encoding and LLM-free visual embeddings to produce a high-recall candidate set, and 2) Vision-adaptive Semantic Refinement, which performs fine-grained semantic matching on top candidates via adaptive region-wise feature fusion.

Result: LightSTAR achieves state-of-the-art retrieval accuracy while reducing end-to-end latency by several-fold.

Conclusion: The proposed LightSTAR framework offers a highly practical solution to the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in visual document retrieval.

Abstract: Visual document retrieval requires rapidly locating relevant pages from large multi-modal corpora in response to user queries. While recent methods powered by Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show competitive accuracy, they suffer from prohibitive computational costs by applying intensive MLLM encoding to every single page. Meanwhile, we observe that user queries are typically keyword-anchored, containing semantically rich words that are expected to appear directly in the visible text of relevant pages, offering an efficient cue for quickly narrowing down candidate pages. Building on this insight, we propose LightSTAR, an efficient framework that decomposes visual document retrieval into: 1) LLM-free Visual Selection, which utilizes content-grounded query encoding to focus on informative words and employs LLM-free visual embeddings to produce a high-recall candidate set; and 2) Vision-adaptive Semantic Refinement, which further performs fine-grained semantic matching exclusively on these top candidates via adaptive region-wise feature fusion to effectively combine textual and layout cues, optimized through a hardness-aware contrastive objective. Experimental results demonstrate that LightSTAR achieves state-of-the-art retrieval accuracy while reducing end-to-end latency by several-fold, offering a highly practical solution to the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in visual document retrieval. Code is available at https://github.com/bokufa/LightSTAR.

</details>


### [271] [AwakeForest: An Interactive Geospatial Platform for Large-Scale Forest Imagery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23542)
*Suraj Prasai,Kangning Cui,Rongkun Zhu,Sarra Alqahtani,Ying Zhang,Victor Paul Pauca,Miles R. Silman,Fan Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: AwakeForest is a platform for large-scale forest imagery analysis that integrates model-assisted inference, automatic annotation, and human-in-the-loop refinement.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Practitioners lack a unified tool for end-to-end workflows in forest imagery analysis that is geospatial-native, cloud-optimized, and ML-integrated.

Method: AwakeForest platform integrates pretrained models, automatic annotation, and human-in-the-loop refinement for scalable interaction with large forest imagery.

Result: AwakeForest produces analysis-ready outputs for downstream analysis and supports iterative model and annotation updates on new scenes.

Conclusion: AwakeForest supports practical forest management and analysis with an end-to-end workflow, demonstrated on the PALMS dataset.

Abstract: Forest imagery analysis often involves multiple tightly coupled vision tasks, which must be performed under substantial variation in geographic regions, sensors, and acquisition conditions. However, practitioners often lack a unified tool that is geospatial-native, cloud-optimized, and ML-integrated for end-to-end workflows spanning annotation, prediction, visualization, and downstream analysis at scale. We present AwakeForest, an interactive end-to-end platform designed for large-scale forest imagery that integrates model-assisted inference, automatic annotation, and human-in-the-loop refinement within a single workflow. Our platform supports plug-and-play integration of pretrained models and enables scalable interaction with forest imagery ranging from standard aerial scenes to large orthomosaics that can span several gigabytes to hundreds of gigabytes. AwakeForest produces analysis-ready outputs that can be directly used for downstream analysis and to support iterative model and annotation updates on new scenes. We demonstrate the system on the PALMS dataset and illustrate how AwakeForest supports an end-to-end workflow for practical forest management and analysis.

</details>


### [272] [Dense Reward for Multi-View 3D Reasoning with Global Maps and Local Views](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23557)
*Jiho Choi,Seonho Lee,Seojeong Park,Hyunjung Shim*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A new framework, DR-MV3D, is proposed for multi-view 3D visual question answering, which uses dense rewards to supervise the reasoning process, leading to improved performance over existing baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current multimodal LLMs for multi-view 3D visual question answering are typically trained with sparse supervision, leading to inconsistent cross-view reasoning and brittle view selection.

Method: The proposed DR-MV3D framework decomposes multi-view 3D visual question answering into three stages: allocentric global map construction, question-conditioned view-trajectory planning, and egocentric grounding for answer prediction, and uses two rewards: a global consistency reward and a local trajectory reward, to supervise the process.

Result: Experiments on MindCube, VSI-Bench, and BLINK (MV) show that DR-MV3D consistently improves over strong multi-image baselines.

Conclusion: The proposed DR-MV3D framework effectively improves multi-view 3D visual question answering by providing dense, verifiable rewards to supervise the reasoning process.

Abstract: Multi-view 3D Visual Question Answering (MV3D-VQA) requires integrating partial observations into a coherent 3D scene representation and selecting informative viewpoints for multi-step spatial reasoning. However, current multimodal LLMs are typically trained with sparse, answer-level supervision, which often yields inconsistent cross-view reasoning and brittle view selection. We present DR-MV3D (Dense Reward for MV3D-VQA), a map-grounded learning framework that provides dense, verifiable rewards to supervise the reasoning process. Our approach decomposes MV3D-VQA into (i) allocentric global map construction, (ii) question-conditioned view-trajectory planning, and (iii) egocentric grounding for answer prediction. To make intermediate steps learnable without manual annotations, we introduce two rewards: a global consistency reward that aligns the predicted map with geometry-consistent pseudo targets from frozen 3D vision foundation models (e.g., VGGT + SAM3), and a local trajectory reward that supervises ordered viewpoint selection. We optimize the full pipeline with trajectory-level policy optimization (GRPO). Experiments on MindCube, VSI-Bench, and BLINK (MV) show that DR-MV3D consistently improves over strong multi-image baselines, supporting the effectiveness of process-level dense supervision for multi-view 3D reasoning.

</details>


### [273] [Polycepta: Object-Centric Appearance Estimation for Multi-Object Tracking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23604)
*Mohamed Nagy,Naoufel Werghi,Jorge Dias,Majid Khonji*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Polycepta, a novel object-centric framework, improves multi-object tracking by recursively estimating object appearance states, leading to state-of-the-art performance and real-time processing.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current tracking-by-detection methods in multi-object tracking (MOT) rely on static appearance descriptors that are frame-independent and often computationally intensive, limiting their robustness and real-time applicability.

Method: Polycepta reformulates appearance modeling as a recursive estimation problem, constructing and updating independent appearance states for each tracked object, and uses a proposed learning strategy to learn object-specific representations.

Result: Polycepta achieves state-of-the-art performance on the KITTI benchmark with a MOTA of 92.27%, operates at 90.57 Hz, and demonstrates consistent improvements in tracking performance and reductions in identity switches on KITTI, Waymo Open Dataset, and MOT17.

Conclusion: Polycepta offers a robust and efficient solution for multi-object tracking by improving appearance estimation through recursive state estimation, leading to enhanced tracking performance and real-time capabilities.

Abstract: The tracking-by-detection paradigm in multi-object tracking (MOT) typically relies on static appearance descriptors to complement motion estimation. However, these descriptors are frame-independent, limiting their robustness as visual cues. Since such descriptors are often obtained from computationally intensive pretrained backbones, real-time MOT systems frequently abandon appearance cues altogether and rely solely on motion prediction and geometric association. In this work, we introduce Polycepta, an object-centric appearance state estimation framework that reformulates appearance modeling as a recursive estimation problem rather than a frame-wise matching task. Polycepta constructs and continuously updates an independent appearance state for each tracked object, enabling future appearance representations to be estimated from accumulated observations. Polycepta is encouraged to learn the appearance-state construction of object-specific representations rather than memorize them through a proposed learning strategy, enabling appearance estimation for unseen classes. A key property of Polycepta is that the quality of appearance estimation improves as object states evolve during inference. While conventional appearance descriptors remain static or degrade over time, Polycepta progressively refines appearance estimates as additional observations are accumulated. Extensive experiments on KITTI, the Waymo Open Dataset, and MOT17 demonstrate consistent reductions in identity switches and improvements in tracking performance when integrated into the tracking-by-detection pipelines. Polycepta operates at 90.57 Hz and delivers state-of-the-art performance on the KITTI benchmark when integrated into the RobMOT framework, achieving a MOTA of 92.27\%.

</details>


### [274] [Vera: A Layered Diffusion Model for Content-Preserving Video Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23610)
*Hongkai Zheng,Ta-Ying Cheng,Benjamin Klein,Yisong Yue,Zhuoning Yuan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A new video editing framework called Vera is introduced, which uses a layered diffusion approach to preserve content while editing videos.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Content preservation remains a challenge in video generation and editing, as existing methods often alter elements that should remain unchanged.

Method: Vera uses a layered diffusion framework, generating an edit layer and alpha matte for compositing with the source video, and a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture for coherent composition.

Result: Vera outperforms leading open-source video editing models in content preservation while remaining competitive in edit quality, using 486K frames of layered training data.

Conclusion: The proposed Vera framework effectively addresses the challenge of content preservation in video editing, offering a more precise and controlled editing process.

Abstract: Video diffusion models have enabled remarkable progress in video generation and editing. However, content preservation remains a core challenge: existing methods regenerate every pixel and often alter elements that should remain unchanged, such as characters or background scenes. We introduce Vera, a layered diffusion framework for content-preserving video editing. Instead of regenerating the entire video, Vera generates an edit layer along with an alpha matte for compositing with the source video, separating creative editing from content preservation by design. To encourage coherent composition with the source video, we extend the text-to-video DiT into a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture, with separate DiTs for each layer that interact through joint self-attention. To support the training of Vera, we further construct a high-quality layered dataset with accurate alpha mattes, diverse scenes and dynamics, and visual effects. Across our quantitative benchmark and human preference study, Vera outperforms leading open-source video editing models in content preservation while remaining competitive in edit quality, using 486K frames of layered training data.

</details>


### [275] [Data Selection Through Iterative Self-Filtering for Vision-Language Settings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23611)
*Andrei Liviu Nicolicioiu,Sarvjeet Singh Ghotra,Morgane M. Moss,Aaron Courville*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A novel method called Self-Filtering is proposed to improve the quality of training data for vision-language models by iteratively filtering and selecting samples.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The availability of large amounts of clean data is crucial for training neural networks, but manual oversight is impractical at large scales, resulting in noisy datasets.

Method: The proposed Self-Filtering method involves training a CLIP model on an evolving, self-selected dataset that balances filtered clean samples and diverse samples from the entire distribution.

Result: Training on vision-language datasets filtered by the proposed approach improves downstream performance without the need for additional data or pre-trained models.

Conclusion: The Self-Filtering method offers a novel approach to mitigating the issue of noisy datasets in vision-language model training, achieving improved performance without relying on heuristics, curated datasets, or pre-trained models.

Abstract: The availability of large amounts of clean data is paramount to training neural networks. However, at large scales, manual oversight is impractical, resulting in sizeable datasets that can be very noisy. Attempts to mitigate this obstacle to producing performant vision-language models have so far involved heuristics, curated reference datasets, and using pre-trained models. Here we propose a novel, bootstrapped method in which a CLIP model is trained on an evolving, self-selected dataset. This evolving dataset constitutes a balance of filtered, highly probable clean samples as well as diverse samples from the entire distribution. Our proposed Self-Filtering method iterates between training the model and selecting a subsequently improved data mixture. Training on vision-language datasets filtered by the proposed approach improves downstream performance without the need for additional data or pre-trained models.

</details>


### [276] [Hedgementation = Hedgerow Segmentation: A Remote Sensing Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23615)
*Nathan Senyard,Salem Hamdani,Astrid Zhang,Derek Wang,Evan Shelhamer,Mathias Lécuyer,Joséphine Gantois*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A new benchmark, Hedgementation, is proposed to evaluate machine learning models for mapping hedgerows from remote sensing data at a country scale.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need to evaluate machine learning models for hedgerow mapping from remote sensing data at a country scale and high spatial resolution.

Method: Combining and harmonizing multiple remote sensing data products and ground truth labels to create a benchmark, and testing supervised and self-supervised learning approaches.

Result: The benchmark and baseline results are provided, with code available for reproduction.

Conclusion: The proposed benchmark, Hedgementation, provides a new standard for evaluating machine learning models for hedgerow mapping.

Abstract: We propose Hedgementation: a new benchmark to evaluate machine learning models for hedgerow mapping from remote sensing data at country scale and 10m$^2$ spatial resolution. We combine and harmonize multiple remote sensing data products and ground truth labels sourced from a hedgerow inventory in France. We measure the ability of three baseline models to generalize across spatial distance, and across climatic zones, a more explicitly challenging task. Our benchmark tests both supervised and self-supervised learning approaches for remote sensing, applied to tracking fine-scale features of high agricultural importance. The code to reproduce the benchmark and baselines results is available at https://github.com/hedgementation/hedgementation.

</details>


### [277] [Pose Anything Anywhere:Model-free Object Poses from Arbitrary References](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23634)
*Hongli Xu,Jiaqi Hu,Junwen Huang,Boyang Zhong,Peter KT Yu,Nassir Navab,Benjamin Busam,Slobodan Ilic*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PANY, a model-free framework, estimates 6D poses of unseen objects from RGB or RGB-D inputs with one or sparse reference views, outperforming existing methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Estimating 6D poses of unseen objects is challenging for open-world robotics and embodied perception due to limitations of model-based and model-free approaches.

Method: PANY uses a multi-view transformer geometry backbone to learn view-consistent geometry and cross-view alignment cues, with pose-graph canonical registration for assist views.

Result: PANY achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, improving pose accuracy by +12% on YCB-V and over +20% on LM-O.

Conclusion: PANY provides a robust solution for estimating 6D poses of unseen objects in real-world environments with strong performance under single-reference and sparse-reference settings.

Abstract: Estimating the 6D pose of unseen objects is a fundamental yet challenging problem for open-world robotics and embodied perception. Model-based methods are accurate but depend on CAD assets or heavy onboarding, while most model-free approaches are still limited to pairwise single-anchor matching and thus fail under occlusion and large viewpoint changes with low query-reference overlap. Therefore, we present PANY, a unified model-free framework that seamlessly supports both RGB and RGB-D inputs, operates on one or sparse pose-free reference views, and generalizes effectively to novel objects. Built on a multi-view transformer geometry backbone, PANY moves beyond pairwise matching by learning view-consistent geometry and cross-view alignment cues that remain stable under wide baselines and limited overlap. When additional unposed assist views are available, PANY aggregates them via pose-graph canonical registration to increase geometric coverage and reinforce the final pose. Extensive experiments show that PANY achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks, substantially outperforming existing model-free methods, improving pose accuracy by +12% on YCB-V and over +20% on LM-O. Furthermore, PANY consistently performs well under both single-reference and sparse-reference settings, demonstrating strong robustness in real-world environments.

</details>


### [278] [Lightweight Neural Framework for Robust 3D Volume and Surface Estimation from Multi-View Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23653)
*Diego E. Farchione,Ramzi Idoughi,Peter Wonka*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A new framework for estimating volume and surface area from multi-view images is proposed, outperforming existing methods, especially with sparse data.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Accurate volume and surface area estimation is crucial for various applications, but existing methods are computationally expensive and perform poorly with sparse and noisy data.

Method: A fully feed-forward framework that uses a graph-based decoder to fuse 3D point cloud reconstructions with 2D features from multi-view images.

Result: The proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods, providing a robust and adaptable solution for quantitative shape analysis, validated across coral monitoring, dietary analysis, and anthropometry.

Conclusion: The proposed framework offers a high-speed, scalable alternative for precise geometric estimation from visual data, maintaining high performance even in resource-constrained or sparse-view scenarios.

Abstract: Accurate volume and surface area estimation is critical for diverse applications, from marine ecology to medical diagnostics. However, existing methods often suffer from high computational costs and poor performance with sparse and noisy data. We propose a fully feed-forward framework that regresses scale-normalized volume and surface area and their associated uncertainties directly from multi-view images. By fusing 3D point cloud reconstructions with view-aligned 2D features through a graph-based decoder, our model bypasses iterative optimization, ensuring exceptional scalability and rapid inference. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly when operating with a low number of input images. Validated across coral monitoring, dietary analysis, and anthropometry, our proposed framework provides a robust, adaptable solution for quantitative shape analysis. This architecture provides a high-speed, scalable alternative for precise geometric estimation from visual data, maintaining high performance even in resource-constrained or sparse-view scenarios.

</details>


### [279] [GeoFidelity-Bench: Evaluating Segment-Level Geographic Fidelity in Text-to-Image Street-View Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23669)
*Kaizhen Tan,Hanzhe Hong,Siru Tao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces GeoFidelity-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating the geographic fidelity of text-to-image models in generating street views for specific road segments. It finds that while adding local names improves plausibility, a gap remains between generating plausible city streets and faithful segment generation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to assess whether text-to-image models can generate street views that correspond to a requested road segment rather than a generic city prior.

Method: The authors introduce a reference-panel benchmark, GeoFidelity-Bench, which contains 7,117 curated Mapillary images covering 109 named OpenStreetMap road segments. They evaluate six open-weight text-to-image generators under different prompts.

Result: The results show that adding street and neighborhood names improves top-1 retrieval accuracy by 5.5 percentage points, but the similarity margin between the target and the nearest segment in the same city remains near zero. GPS coordinates yield no statistically clear additional benefit.

Conclusion: The paper concludes that there is a persistent gap between city- or neighborhood-plausible street-view generation and faithful generation for a specific road segment, highlighting the need for further improvement in text-to-image models.

Abstract: Text-to-image models can generate visually plausible city streets, but whether their outputs correspond to a requested road segment rather than a generic city prior remains unclear. We introduce GeoFidelity-Bench, a reference-panel benchmark for segment-conditioned geographic fidelity in street-view generation. It contains 7,117 curated Mapillary images covering 109 named OpenStreetMap road segments in 25 cities across six continents. For each generated panel, the benchmark ranks the target reference panel against panels from the nearest segment in the same city, other segments in the same city, and segments from other cities, making local discrimination rather than absolute target similarity the primary test. We evaluate six open-weight text-to-image generators under city-only, street-and-neighborhood, and GPS-augmented prompts. Adding street and neighborhood names is associated with an increase of 5.5 percentage points in top-1 retrieval accuracy over city-only prompts, with a 95% confidence interval from 3.4 to 7.7 percentage points. However, the similarity margin between the target and the nearest segment in the same city remains near zero, indicating that local names improve broad local plausibility more than exact segment identity. Prompts that keep the city fixed but use incorrect street or neighborhood names further show that only part of the gain depends on the correct local names, while appending raw GPS coordinates as ordinary text yields no statistically clear additional benefit. Held-out real-image queries successfully recover segment identity, showing that the curated references contain usable segment-level signal. GeoFidelity-Bench thus reveals a persistent gap between city- or neighborhood-plausible street-view generation and faithful generation for a specific road segment.

</details>


### [280] [IMAGIN-4D: Image-Guided Controllable Interaction Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23675)
*Sai Kumar Dwivedi,Federica Bogo,Buğra Tekin,Chenhongyi Yang,Nadine Bertsch,Tomas Hodan,Michael J. Black,Dimitrios Tzionas,Shreyas Hampali*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: IMAGIN-4D, a diffusion-based HOI generator that uses a reference image to improve fine-grained interaction control in human-object interaction (HOI) generation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current HOI generation methods are ambiguous and can produce different results for the same prompt and trajectory. The authors aim to address this limitation by introducing a visual specification in the form of a reference image.

Method: IMAGIN-4D decomposes image conditioning spatio-temporally, extracting supervised interaction-state tokens and computing frame-aware tokens to balance image, text, and waypoint cues.

Result: Experiments on FBM and BEHAVE datasets show that IMAGIN-4D improves fine-grained interaction control over single-token and uniformly image-conditioned baselines while preserving waypoint-following and motion quality.

Conclusion: IMAGIN-4D offers a novel approach to HOI generation by leveraging reference images to enhance interaction control, paving the way for more realistic and varied human-object interactions in applications like character animation, robotics, and AR/VR.

Abstract: Generating human-object interactions (HOI) is central to character animation, robotics, AR/VR, and embodied AI. Recent HOI generation methods synthesize motion from text, object geometry, and sparse waypoints, controlling action semantics and object trajectories. However, these signals underspecify interaction: the same prompt and trajectory can produce different grasps, approach directions, body poses, object poses, contacts, and body-object layouts. We address this ambiguity with a reference image as a visual specification of the desired interaction snapshot. However, a single global image representation conflates distinct cues and conditions all frames on identical visual evidence. We therefore introduce IMAGIN-4D, a diffusion-based HOI generator that decomposes image conditioning spatio-temporally. For spatial conditioning, IMAGIN-4D extracts supervised interaction-state tokens for body pose, object pose, body-object contact, and spatial relationships at the depicted frame. For temporal conditioning, it computes frame-aware tokens by querying image patches per generated frame, allowing sequence segments to attend to different visual cues from the same image. To balance image, text, and waypoint cues, IMAGIN-4D uses role-aware conditioning: text, waypoints, and interaction-state tokens use separate AdaLN streams, while frame-aware visual tokens cross-attend with motion tokens. Since HOI motion datasets lack paired images, we build a synthetic motion-to-image rendering pipeline from FullBodyManipulation (FBM) and introduce an image-adherence metric to evaluate whether generated motions match the reference snapshot. Experiments on FBM and BEHAVE show that IMAGIN-4D improves fine-grained interaction control over single-token and uniformly image-conditioned baselines while preserving waypoint-following and motion quality. Code and models will be released at https://imagin4d.github.io.

</details>


### [281] [AIR: Adaptive Interleaved Reasoning with Code in MLLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23678)
*Cong Han,Xiaohan Lan,Haibo Qiu,Yujie Zhong*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper enhances multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with adaptive interleaved reasoning capabilities for numerical computation tasks through reinforcement learning and a proposed three-component solution.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing MLLMs focus on tool-use in vision-perception tasks and rely on predefined heuristics, which are incapable of addressing numerical computation problems.

Method: The paper proposes a three-component solution: a two-stage cold-start data construction pipeline, data filtering strategies for RL dataset curation, and an adaptive tool-invocation strategy with a group-constrained reward function.

Result: The approach improves performance by an average of 6.1 percentage points on evaluation benchmarks, with a 9.9 pp increase in accuracy for interleaved reasoning samples and a tool-use success rate exceeding 95%.

Conclusion: The proposed solution effectively empowers MLLMs with adaptive interleaved reasoning capabilities for numerical computation tasks.

Abstract: Following the paradigm shift initiated by OpenAI o3, interleaved reasoning with code to enhance multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has become a pivotal research frontier. The existing literature focuses primarily on tool-use within vision-perception tasks. However, such approaches typically rely on predefined heuristics for visual manipulation and are inherently incapable of addressing numerical computation problems due to their exclusive focus on visual operations. This paper empowers MLLMs with adaptive interleaved reasoning capabilities through extended reinforcement learning training on code-augmented complex numerical computation tasks. To this end, we propose a comprehensive three-component solution consisting of: a two-stage cold-start data construction pipeline, data filtering strategies for RL dataset curation, and an adaptive tool-invocation strategy leveraging a group-constrained reward function for interleaved reasoning trajectories. Extensive experiments demonstrate that after Reinforcement Learning training with the group-constrained reward function, performance improves by an average of 6.1 percentage points (pp) on evaluation benchmarks. Specifically, the accuracy for interleaved reasoning samples increases by 9.9 pp, and the overall success rate of tool-use exceeds 95%. Our data and code are available at: https://github.com/CongHan0808/AIR.git.

</details>


### [282] [Semantic Browsing: Controllable Diversity for Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23679)
*Sara Dorfman,Maya Vishnevsky,Omer Dahary,Or Patashnik,Daniel Cohen-Or*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces a method for controlled diversity in text-to-image models, enabling users to navigate structured image galleries and experience creative exploration through meaningful axes of variation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing methods to improve diversity in text-to-image models produce outputs driven by incidental variations rather than meaningful design choices, leading to a collapse into a single visual interpretation.

Method: The method involves inducing diversity directly at the text level, leveraging rich textual representations, and employing an agentic workflow to enforce structured variation attuned to the original prompt.

Result: The method produces diverse and navigable design spaces where every variation corresponds to a specific, user-understandable semantic decision.

Conclusion: The paper presents a new approach to controlled diversity in text-to-image models, enabling semantic browsing and creative exploration through structured image galleries.

Abstract: Modern text-to-image models excel in visual fidelity and prompt adherence. However, this strict adherence comes at the cost of diversity: generated samples tend to collapse into a single visual interpretation. Existing methods to improve diversity produce outputs driven by incidental variations rather than meaningful design choices. This motivates a new variant of the diversity task where structure is enforced on the generated samples. We introduce a method for controlled diversity that enables Semantic Browsing, where users can navigate structured image galleries and experience creative exploration through a systematic traversal of meaningful, interpretable axes of variation. Achieving this level of semantic control requires a deep understanding of the scene. We exploit the fact that recent text-to-image models are trained on elaborated captions, effectively decoupling semantic decision-making from pixel generation. This enables a paradigm shift: instead of relying on stochastic variation within the text-to-image model, we induce diversity directly at the text level. By leveraging rich textual representations, we allow a Vision Language Model (VLM) to operate on the full scene context. To overcome the generic outputs typical of standard VLMs, we employ an agentic workflow that explicitly enforces structured variation attuned to the original prompt. We demonstrate that our method produces diverse and navigable design spaces where every variation corresponds to a specific, user-understandable semantic decision.

</details>


### [283] [Keep The Essentials: Efficient Reference Conditioned Generation via Token Dropping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23682)
*Rishubh Parihar,Ayush Raina,R. Venkatesh Babu,Or Patashnik*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces Sparse Context, a method to improve the efficiency of reference-based diffusion models by constructing sparse reference representations, achieving a significant increase in inference speed without compromising visual quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reference-based diffusion models are computationally expensive and their cost scales with the number of input references, making efficiency a crucial but under-explored issue in this realm.

Method: The method involves constructing sparse reference representations by retaining a reduced subset of reference tokens, fine-tuning the model with random token dropping, and applying task-aware token selection strategies at inference time.

Result: The method achieves a 4x increase in inference speed for multi-reference generation and a 2x increase for single reference generation, without compromising visual quality across spatially-aligned editing and subject-driven generation.

Conclusion: The paper presents Sparse Context as an effective approach to enhancing the efficiency of reference-based diffusion models, offering flexible control and significant speedup without sacrificing generation capabilities.

Abstract: Reference-based diffusion models enable highly controllable image generation by leveraging elements from input images to guide prompt-driven synthesis. However, these models are computationally expensive in runtime, and their cost scales severely with the number of input references. While the efficiency of diffusion models has been extensively studied in the context of prompt-driven generation, it remains largely under-explored in the realm of reference-based models. This setting presents unique challenges not addressed by methods focusing solely on generation. In particular, the wasteful representation of references as dense token grids offers significant opportunities for improvement. In this work, we present Sparse Context, a method for constructing sparse reference representations by retaining only a reduced subset of reference tokens. We observe that even without modifying the model, dropping a significant portion of reference tokens at inference time largely preserves its generation capabilities. To fully realize this potential, we fine-tune the model with random token dropping at varying ratios, encouraging robustness to partial reference representations. Crucially, this training strategy decouples the model from any specific token selection rule, allowing flexible control at inference time. At inference time, instead of random dropping, we apply task-aware token selection strategies that prioritize the most informative regions of the reference images, adapting the token budget to the input and task requirements. Extensive experiments show our method achieves a 4x increase in inference speed for multi-reference generation and an 2x for single reference generation. Importantly, this efficiency is achieved without compromising visual quality across both spatially-aligned editing and subject-driven generation.

</details>


### [284] [Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23688)
*Yehonathan Litman,Xiaoxuan Ma,Manan Shah,Nicolas Ugrinovic,Kris Kitani,Fernando De la Torre,Shubham Tulsiani*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework for reconstructing dynamic non-rigid objects from monocular video, addressing limitations of prior approaches.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to improve the reconstruction of dynamic non-rigid objects from monocular video, particularly in complex scenarios with large deformations and occlusions.

Method: The method involves a two-stage approach: (1) adapting a single-view 3D reconstruction model to yield temporally consistent per-frame predictions via causal latent conditioning, and (2) optimizing a deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting representation through an occlusion-aware optimization that leverages a view-conditioned diffusion prior.

Result: The result shows that Lift4D improves over prior 4D reconstruction methods, particularly on challenging in-the-wild sequences with severe occlusions and non-rigid motion.

Conclusion: The conclusion is that Lift4D provides a more effective framework for reconstructing dynamic non-rigid objects from monocular video, handling complex scenarios with large deformations and occlusions.

Abstract: Reconstructing dynamic non-rigid objects from monocular video requires integrating visual cues from direct observations with data-driven priors over geometry and appearance. Prior approaches either learn to directly predict 4D representations from visual input or initialize a 3D representation that is subsequently deformed and refined based on video evidence. However, the former are constrained by the scarcity of 4D training data, while the latter leverage priors only for the initial reconstruction and rely solely on video supervision thereafter; neither handles complex in-the-wild scenarios with large deformations and occlusions well. We present Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework that addresses both limitations. First, we adapt an existing single-view 3D reconstruction model to yield temporally consistent per-frame predictions via causal latent conditioning, providing a coherent initialization for a deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting representation. We then ``sculpt'' this representation to match the input video through an occlusion-aware optimization that faithfully recovers visible surface details while completing unobserved regions using a view-conditioned diffusion prior. We demonstrate that Lift4D clearly improves over prior 4D reconstruction methods, particularly on challenging in-the-wild sequences with severe occlusions and non-rigid motion.

</details>


<div id='cs.CL'></div>

# cs.CL [[Back]](#toc)

### [285] [Less is More: Lightweight Prompt Compression for Question Answering Applications on Edge Devices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20571)
*Zihuai Xu,Ruofei Hou,Yang Xu,Hongli Xu,Yunming Liao,Ying Zhu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: CORE, a two-stage sentence-level prompt compression method, improves accuracy and reduces computational overhead for large language models on edge devices.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing prompt compression methods rely on auxiliary small language models, introducing significant memory and computational overhead, limiting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.

Method: CORE uses named entity recognition, semantic matching, orthogonal residual retrieval, and spatial proximity-based metric to eliminate the need for small language models.

Result: CORE improves accuracy by at least 30.19%, reduces memory usage by at least 50.47%, and achieves at least 1.94 times speedup on edge devices, with a substantial energy reduction of 95.74% on smartphones.

Conclusion: CORE is a practical and generalizable method for mobile deployments, enhancing the response accuracy of large language models while reducing computational overhead.

Abstract: In agent-driven question answering (QA) applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is commonly introduced to enhance the response accuracy of large language models (LLMs) by providing additional context. Due to the inherent noise in retrieval results and the coarse granularity of document-level retrieval, the retrieved context often contains substantial redundant information. In this setting, the agent prompt, consisting of the user query and the associated retrieved context, leads to unnecessary computational overhead during LLM inference. Existing prompt compression methods typically rely on auxiliary small language models (SLMs) to estimate context importance. However, such approaches introduce significant memory and computational overhead, which limits their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. In this paper, we propose CORE, a two-stage sentence-level prompt compression method that eliminates the need for SLMs. In the first stage, CORE constructs an answer set via named entity recognition (NER) and a clue set via semantic matching. In the second stage, CORE refines the clue set using an orthogonal residual retrieval strategy and designs a spatial proximity-based metric to filter the answer set. The two sets are then combined to form the final compressed context. We implement CORE on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge device and a Huawei Nova smartphone. Experimental results demonstrate that within a 2000-token budget, CORE improves accuracy by at least 30.19% compared to state-of-the-art baselines, while reducing memory usage by at least 50.47% and achieving at least 1.94 times speedup on the edge device. Moreover, compared to the state-of-the-art LLMLingua2 method, CORE achieves a substantial energy reduction of 95.74% on the smartphone, highlighting its practicality and generalizability for mobile deployments.

</details>


### [286] [Investigating Linguistic Steering: An Analysis of Adjectival Effects Across Large Language Model Architectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20572)
*Lars Malmqvist*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The paper introduces a framework to analyze how individual adjectives affect Large Language Models' performance, finding that a small subset of adjectives have a significant impact and that models' responses vary based on their architecture and the adjectives' context.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To achieve reliable control of Large Language Models (LLMs), it is necessary to understand how they interpret linguistic cues, specifically the impact of individual adjectives on model performance.

Method: The paper uses Shapley values to quantify the effect of individual adjectives on model performance across various LLMs, including o3, gpt-4o-mini, phi-3, llama-3-70b, and deepseek-r1, on the MMLU benchmark.

Result: The study finds that a small subset of adjectives acts as powerful 'levers' with significant effects on model performance, but these effects are not universal and vary by model lineage and architecture. The steering direction of these adjectives is contingent on their syntactic role and position within the prompt. Larger models exhibit strong, non-additive interaction effects between adjectives, while smaller models respond more literally.

Conclusion: The results highlight the challenge of steering model behavior as models scale, suggesting a need for compositional and model-specific alignment techniques due to the increasing sophistication but also unpredictability of LLMs' interpretation of prompts.

Abstract: Achieving reliable control of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires a precise, scalable understanding of how they interpret linguistic cues. We introduce a rigorous framework using Shapley values to quantify the steering effect of individual adjectives on model performance, moving beyond anecdotal heuristics to principled attribution. Applying this method to 100 adjectives across a diverse suite of models (including o3, gpt-4o-mini, phi-3, llama-3-70b, and deepseek-r1) on the MMLU benchmark, we uncover several critical findings for AI alignment. First, we find that a small subset of adjectives act as disproportionately powerful "levers," yet their effects are not universal. Cross-model analysis reveals a "family effect": models of a shared lineage exhibit correlated sensitivity profiles, while architecturally distinct models react in a largely uncorrelated manner, challenging the notion of a one-size-fits-all prompting strategy. Second, focused follow-up studies demonstrate that the steering direction of these powerful adjectives is not intrinsic but is highly contingent on their syntactic role and position within the prompt. For larger models like gpt-4o-mini, we provide the first quantitative evidence of strong, non-additive interaction effects where adjectives can synergistically amplify, antagonistically dampen, or even reverse each other's impact. In contrast, smaller models like phi-3 exhibit a more literal and less compositional response. These results suggest that as models scale, their interpretation of prompts becomes more sophisticated but also less predictable, posing a significant challenge for robustly steering model behavior and highlighting the need for compositional and model-specific alignment techniques.

</details>


### [287] [Post-Training Recipe, More Than Model Family, Shapes Multi-Agent LLM Conversational Behavior](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20632)
*Luyang Zhang,Jialu Wang,Fei Xue,Yi-Yun Chu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The study examines the behavior of multi-LLM systems, finding that the same family label is an incomplete proxy for conversational diversity, and post-training recipe is a key factor in determining LLM behavior.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The value of multi-LLM systems depends on the models producing measurably different conversational behaviors when given the same input. Prior studies recommend drawing one model per family for behavioral diversity, but it's unclear if this holds in interactive multi-LLM systems.

Method: The study uses a 940,000-chain 11-checkpoint corpus and a 1.6M-chain same-base Llama factorial to examine the behavior of LLMs in interactive multi-LLM systems.

Result: The results show that a reasoning-distilled Llama checkpoint shifts by 18% depending on which same-base partner it replies to, and post-training recipe is a first-class axis for multi-LLM panel composition.

Conclusion: Model family alone is an incomplete proxy for conversational diversity, and post-training recipe is a key factor in determining LLM behavior in multi-LLM systems.

Abstract: Multi-LLM systems use multiple language models to deliberate, judge each other's outputs, or coordinate as agents. Their value depends on the models producing measurably different conversational behaviors when given the same input. Prior offline studies recommend drawing one model per family for behavioral diversity, because LLMs prefer outputs from their own family when rating one another in isolation. Whether the same family label predicts behavior in interactive multi-LLM systems, the setting that real deployed systems use, has not been tested. We study this with a 940,000-chain 11-checkpoint corpus and a 1.6M-chain same-base Llama factorial. On our validated headline metric, hedging, a reasoning-distilled Llama checkpoint shifts by 18% depending on which same-base partner it replies to, more than any cross-family hedging gap in the controlled subset. Qwen, closed-API, and runtime checks suggest the pattern is not isolated, while repair and challenge analyses remain exploratory because their surface-cue detectors are weaker. Overall, the results identify post-training recipe as a first-class axis for multi-LLM panel composition and show that model family alone is an incomplete proxy for conversational diversity.

</details>


### [288] [EmoInstruct-TTS: Dual-Path Instruction-Guided Emotional Speech Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20650)
*Minghui Wu,Ganjun Liu,Zikun Fang,Ting Meng,Hongchuan Wu,Bingao Xu,Yonglong Cai,Jiasheng Chen,Jun Du*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: EmoInstruct-TTS is proposed for controllable speech synthesis with fine-grained emotional control.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing approaches for instruction-based speech synthesis lack fine-grained intensity modeling and rely on coarse emotion labels.

Method: A dual-path framework with Emotion2embed for 48 emotional states and ICE-Flow for inferring embeddings from instructions.

Result: Improved emotional controllability and speech naturalness over strong baselines.

Conclusion: EmoInstruct-TTS enables fine-grained emotional control in speech synthesis through a novel dual-path framework.

Abstract: Instruction-based controllable speech synthesis enables users to specify emotions through natural language. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse emotion labels and lack explicit modeling of fine-grained intensity. We propose EmoInstruct-TTS, a dual-path instruction-guided framework for emotional speech synthesis. We introduce Emotion2embed, a supervised semantic-acoustic emotion embedding covering 48 emotional states, including fine-grained categories and intensity levels. To infer embeddings from free-form instructions, we design an Instruction-Conditioned Emotion Flow Model (ICE-Flow) that generates acoustically grounded emotion representations. The inferred embeddings are integrated into an LLM-based synthesis pipeline to provide explicit emotional control while preserving semantic planning. Experiments show improved emotional controllability and speech naturalness over strong baselines.

</details>


### [289] [Specific Domain Ontology Construction Using Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20691)
*Vivian Magri Alcaldi Soares,Renata Wassermann*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: This paper explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 to automatically construct ontologies, specifically conceptual hierarchies, for a given domain with human-like expertise.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The manual creation of ontologies is labor-intensive, and many domains lack reference ontologies. LLMs have shown a remarkable ability to understand natural language, making them suitable for aiding in ontology development.

Method: The technique involves using LLMs as domain experts to build conceptual hierarchies from an initial concept. The experiment was conducted in the domain of the Brazilian maritime territory (Blue Amazon) using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.

Result: Twenty ontologies were automatically constructed and evaluated by human experts. The models produced coherent conceptualizations but required refinement to be satisfactory representations of the domain.

Conclusion: The study demonstrates the potential of LLMs in aiding ontology development, particularly in constructing conceptual hierarchies. However, the results also highlight the need for further refinement to achieve satisfactory domain representations.

Abstract: Ontologies are useful structures to organize and maintain information that can be understood both by humans and systems. However, since their manual crafting is a laborious task, many specific domains lack reference ontologies. The outstanding ability for understanding natural language demonstrated by the Large Language Models (LLMs) has motivated their application to aid on a variety of fields, including on ontology development. This work presents the experimentation with a technique that uses LLMs in the role of domain experts to build conceptual hierarchies for a given initial concept. Twenty ontologies automatically constructed for the domain of the Brazilian maritime territory (a.k.a the Blue Amazon) using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were then evaluated by human experts. The models were able to construct overall coherent conceptualizations of the domain, but none of the outputs was completely satisfactory as a representation of the context without refinement.

</details>


### [290] [MindAlign: Decoding Inner Speech from fMRI Signals via Multimodal Embedding Alignment under Limited Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20696)
*Muxuan Liu,Ichiro Kobayashi,Satoshi Nishida*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A new brain-to-language framework called MindAlign is proposed, enabling open-ended text generation from fMRI signals without modifying the underlying language model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Decoding inner speech from non-invasive brain signals is challenging due to the absence of overt linguistic output, limited training data, and large inter-subject variability.

Method: MindAlign, a decoupled two-stage brain-to-language framework, which first learns a subject-specific neural-semantic alignment and then integrates it with visual context to prompt a frozen multimodal language model.

Result: The proposed approach consistently outperforms fMRI-only and random baselines, and the learned semantic-to-language projection can generalize across subjects.

Conclusion: The results support a scalable and modular direction for brain-to-text decoding, indicating that neural signals modulate semantic content beyond image-driven priors.

Abstract: Decoding inner speech from non-invasive brain signals remains a fundamental challenge due to the absence of overt linguistic output, limited training data, and large inter-subject variability. Existing brain-to-text approaches often rely on task-specific decoder fine-tuning, which restricts scalability and complicates adaptation to new participants. We propose MindAlign, a decoupled two-stage brain-to-language framework that enables open-ended text generation from fMRI signals without modifying the underlying language model. The first stage learns a subject-specific neural-semantic alignment that maps fMRI activity into a shared multimodal semantic space, extracting a latent semantic sketch of the internally generated sentence. The second stage integrates this sketch with visual context to prompt a frozen multimodal language model for free-form generation. Experiments on fMRI data collected during silent image description demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms fMRI-only and random baselines. We further show that the learned semantic-to-language projection can generalize across subjects, enabling effective decoding when paired with subject-specific neural alignment. These results indicate that neural signals modulate semantic content beyond image-driven priors, supporting a scalable and modular direction for brain-to-text decoding.

</details>


### [291] [VeriBound: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bounds for Process Reward Models Trained with Formal Verification Tools](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20740)
*Amirul Rahman,Mohammed Sabih Alsharari*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The paper proposes VeriBound, a theoretical framework providing PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds for Process Reward Models (PRMs) trained with formal verification tools, addressing the lack of theoretical explanation for their cross-task generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The training data acquisition for Process Reward Models (PRMs) is a bottleneck due to costly human annotation and noisy Monte Carlo roll-out estimates. Although FOVER uses formal verification tools for automatic annotation, the generalization phenomenon lacks a theoretical explanation.

Method: The authors propose VeriBound, a theoretical framework that establishes PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds, sample complexity results, convergence analysis, and error propagation bounds for PRMs trained with formal verification tools.

Result: The framework provides four main results: (i) a PAC-Bayesian generalization bound relating empirical verification error to expected error, (ii) a sample complexity result of $O(d \log(d/δ) / ε^2)$ examples, (iii) a convergence analysis proving linear convergence under certain conditions, and (iv) an error propagation bound relating step-level verification error to Best-of-K performance degradation.

Conclusion: VeriBound provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the generalization behavior of PRMs trained with formal verification tools, filling the gap in theoretical explanations for their cross-task generalization phenomenon.

Abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) provide step-level verification for Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, yet their training data acquisition remains a bottleneck: human annotation is costly and Monte Carlo roll-out estimates are noisy.
